title: Effects of gender and regional dialect on prosodic patterns in American English
features_measured: speaking rate (syll/s), pause frequency and duration (>100 ms), ToBI pitch accents and boundary tones
key_finding_with_numbers: Northern vs Southern US speakers (and gender) differ in prosody; measured on 40 read passages with ToBI. Group values UNVERIFIED in this summary.
graphable_signature: Speaking rate and pitch-accent distribution by region
why_it_matters_for_sound_local: Prosodic cues are phone-robust.

title: Regional variation in temporal organization in American English
key_finding_with_numbers: Regional variation in temporal organisation of American English. Numbers UNVERIFIED.
why_it_matters_for_sound_local: Timing cues.

title: Prosodic and segmental cues to regional dialect variation in American English
venue: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
features_measured: articulation rate, pauses, pitch accents, boundary tones, nPVI; free classification
key_finding_with_numbers: Regional dialect affects articulation rate, pauses, pitch accents, boundary tones and syllable duration variability; listeners from Ohio and Texas grouped 60 talkers using unmodified, monotone and low-pass filtered speech.
graphable_signature: Free-classification clustering of talkers; F0-flattened vs filtered conditions
why_it_matters_for_sound_local: Shows how much "accent" survives without segments (prosody-only).

title: Between-speaker and within-speaker variation in speech tempo of American English
venue: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
key_finding_with_numbers: 192 speakers from Wisconsin and North Carolina: Wisconsin speakers speak faster with shorter phrases; tempo fastest in the 40s; men faster than women.
why_it_matters_for_sound_local: Speaking rate needs age/sex normalisation.

title: Acoustic characteristics of the vowel systems of six regional varieties of American English
venue: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
key_finding_with_numbers: 48 talkers, both genders, six US regions (NSP), five repetitions of 11 vowels: acoustic regional differences.
graphable_signature: Six-region vowel charts (New England, Mid-Atlantic, North, Midland, South, West)
why_it_matters_for_sound_local: Directly comparable six-region acoustic baseline in hVd.

title: Some acoustic cues for the perceptual categorization of American English regional dialects
key_finding_with_numbers: Experiment 1 identified phonetic features distinguishing dialects; Experiment 2 naive listeners categorised talkers into six regions. Accuracy UNVERIFIED.
why_it_matters_for_sound_local: Human benchmark for regional classification.

title: Homebodies and army brats: Some effects of early linguistic experience and residential history on dialect categorization
key_finding_with_numbers: "Army brats" (lived in 3+ states) categorised regions more accurately than "homebodies"; experience with a region helped for that region. Accuracy UNVERIFIED.
why_it_matters_for_sound_local: Exposure matters: human judges vary.

title: Free classification of regional dialects of American English
key_finding_with_numbers: Naive listeners perform poorly in forced-choice categorisation; free classification reveals perceptual groupings. Numbers UNVERIFIED.
why_it_matters_for_sound_local: Use coarse regional buckets.

title: The Nationwide Speech Project: A new corpus of American English dialects
key_finding_with_numbers: Nationwide Speech Project: nearly an hour of speech from each of 60 talkers across six regions.
why_it_matters_for_sound_local: Licensable training/testing corpus (LDC2007S15).

title: Perceptual and Phonetic Experiments on American English Dialect Identification
venue: Journal of Language and Social Psychology
key_finding_with_numbers: Perceptual and phonetic experiments on dialect identification. Numbers UNVERIFIED.
why_it_matters_for_sound_local: Short-prompt identification.

title: Unsupervised Discriminative Training With Application to Dialect Classification
venue: IEEE Transactions on Audio, Speech and Language Processing
key_finding_with_numbers: Unsupervised discriminative training for dialect classification. Corpora and accuracies UNVERIFIED.
why_it_matters_for_sound_local: Machine dialect-ID baseline.

title: ACCDIST: a metric for comparing speakers' accents
topic: Accent distance and perception (validated against listeners)
what_it_measured: ACCDIST: correlates each speaker's table of inter-segment spectral distances with accent-group tables, so the score reflects pronunciation system not voice.
key_finding_with_numbers: 274 speakers (10 M + 10 F per area, 20 shared sentences) from 14 accent areas; 11% classification error, half the error of a direct spectral-distance metric (full text checked).
why_it_matters_for_sound_local: Blueprint for a speaker-normalised "how local" score: compare the learner's own vowel-to-vowel distance pattern with a local reference pattern, which cancels mic and voice differences.
region: Accent distance and perception (validated against listeners)

title: Human and computer recognition of regional accents and ethnic groups from British English speech
authors: Hanani, A.; Russell, M.J.; Carey, M.J.
topic: Accent distance and perception (validated against listeners)
accents: 14 British regional accents; British ethnic groups (incl. British Asian)
what_it_measured: Human listeners vs automatic language-ID-style systems on regional accent and ethnic group from British English speech.
key_finding_with_numbers: Systems did much better on a 12-class language task and a 2-class ethnic-group task than on 14-class regional accent (abstract). Human-vs-machine accuracy figures UNVERIFIED.
why_it_matters_for_sound_local: Shows regional accent is harder to detect than L1/ethnic background, so Sound Local needs targeted segmental features, not a generic accent-ID model.
region: Accent distance and perception (validated against listeners)

title: Automatic sociophonetics: Exploring corpora with a forensic accent recognition system
venue: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
topic: Accent distance and perception (validated against listeners)
what_it_measured: Y-ACCDIST forensic accent recognition used as a sociophonetic exploration tool.
key_finding_with_numbers: Classified speakers by region/language background, produced clusters matching local social networks and ranked which phonemes carry most accent information (abstract). Accuracy numbers UNVERIFIED.
why_it_matters_for_sound_local: Ranking phonemes by accent information tells the game which words/vowels to put in a level.
region: Accent distance and perception (validated against listeners)

title: Perceptive evaluation of Levenshtein dialect distance measurements using Norwegian dialect data
topic: Accent distance and perception (validated against listeners)
what_it_measured: Levenshtein (string) dialect distances vs distances judged by native listeners.
key_finding_with_numbers: Correlates computed Levenshtein distances with listener-judged distances for 15 dialects (abstract). Correlation value UNVERIFIED.
why_it_matters_for_sound_local: Classic proof that an automatic phonetic distance can track what listeners hear as "different"; the validation design Sound Local should copy.
region: Accent distance and perception (validated against listeners)

title: Measuring Norwegian dialect distances using acoustic features
authors: Heeringa, Wilbert; Johnson, Keith; Gooskens, Charlotte
topic: Accent distance and perception (validated against listeners)
what_it_measured: Fully acoustic (no transcription) dialect distances vs traditional dialectology and listener perception.
key_finding_with_numbers: Tests whether acoustic-only measures approximate transcription-based and perceptual distances (abstract). Correlations UNVERIFIED.
why_it_matters_for_sound_local: Sound Local has audio, not transcriptions; this is the evidence base for acoustic-only distance.
region: Accent distance and perception (validated against listeners)

title: Inducing a measure of phonetic similarity from pronunciation variation
authors: Wieling, Martijn; Margaretha, Eliza; Nerbonne, John
topic: Accent distance and perception (validated against listeners)
what_it_measured: Induces segment-to-segment phonetic distances from pronunciation alternations via alignment + pointwise mutual information.
key_finding_with_numbers: Method applied to six dialect atlases; induced distances relate to acoustic vowel distances (abstract). Correlation values UNVERIFIED.
why_it_matters_for_sound_local: Gives data-driven costs for substitutions (e.g. how bad /t/ vs [ʔ] is) instead of hand-set penalties.
region: Accent distance and perception (validated against listeners)

title: Advances in Dialectometry
topic: Accent distance and perception (validated against listeners)
what_it_measured: Review of computational and statistical dialectometry methods.
key_finding_with_numbers: Review; no single headline number.
why_it_matters_for_sound_local: Map of which distance methods have been validated, useful before choosing the scoring metric.
region: Accent distance and perception (validated against listeners)

title: Formant frequencies of vowels in 13 accents of the British Isles
venue: Journal of the International Phonetic Association
topic: Accent distance and perception (validated against listeners)
accents: 13 accents of the British Isles incl. Glasgow, London
what_it_measured: Semi-automatic F1/F2 of vowels from male speakers in 13 accents; z-scored Bark and Hz.
key_finding_with_numbers: Acoustic vowel data for 13 accents with discussion of automatic formant-measurement pitfalls (abstract). Per-vowel values in paper (UNVERIFIED here).
why_it_matters_for_sound_local: Reference vowel targets for Glasgow and London from one consistent method.
region: Accent distance and perception (validated against listeners)

title: Vowel normalization for accent: An investigation of best exemplar locations in northern and southern British English sentences
venue: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
topic: Accent distance and perception (validated against listeners)
what_it_measured: Listeners' best-exemplar vowel locations after carrier sentences in different accents.
key_finding_with_numbers: Listeners shifted vowel categorisation to match the carrier sentence accent; shift depended on language background and regional experience (abstract). Effect sizes UNVERIFIED.
why_it_matters_for_sound_local: Listeners judge a vowel relative to the rest of the accent, so the score should judge vowels relative to the player's own system.
region: Accent distance and perception (validated against listeners)

title: Plasticity in vowel perception and production: A study of accent change in young adults
venue: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
accents: Northern vs Southern British English (university students)
what_it_measured: Production and perception of vowels in students tracked over two years after moving.
key_finding_with_numbers: Students changed their accent over two years; production related to perception, but perception did not reliably change over time (abstract). Size of change UNVERIFIED.
why_it_matters_for_sound_local: Real-world evidence of how much adults can shift an accent and over what timescale; sets expectations for levels.

title: Imitation Improves Language Comprehension
authors: Adank, Patti; Hagoort, Peter; Bekkering, Harold
what_it_measured: Comprehension after imitating vs listening, repeating in own accent, or transcribing.
key_finding_with_numbers: Imitating the accent improved comprehension more than the other three conditions (abstract). Effect sizes UNVERIFIED.
why_it_matters_for_sound_local: Direct support for the game loop itself: speaking in the accent helps understanding.

title: Accent imitation positively affects language attitudes
authors: Adank, Patti; Stewart, Andrew J.; Connell, Louise; Wood, Jeffrey
what_it_measured: Attitudes to a Glaswegian speaker after imitating vs repeating.
key_finding_with_numbers: 52 participants (full text); imitation increased social-attractiveness ratings vs repeating without imitation (abstract). Effect sizes UNVERIFIED.
why_it_matters_for_sound_local: Glaswegian stimuli; supports the "kind, never mocking" brief: imitating an accent increases warmth toward its speakers.

title: Dialect Acquisition
accents: Canadian English speakers moving to southern England
what_it_measured: Second-dialect acquisition by Canadian children in southern England.
key_finding_with_numbers: Proposes eight principles of dialect acquisition (e.g. lexical before phonological, simple rules before complex) (abstract).
why_it_matters_for_sound_local: Predicts which accent features learners pick up first; orders Sound Local's difficulty curve. Chambers is UofT.

title: Second Dialect Acquisition: A Sociophonetic Perspective
what_it_measured: Review of second-dialect acquisition from a sociophonetic perspective.
key_finding_with_numbers: Acquisition changes specific features, shaped by linguistic, social and developmental factors (abstract).
why_it_matters_for_sound_local: Up-to-date summary of which features adult learners can change.

title: Adolescents, Young Adults, and the Critical Period: Two Case Studies from “Seven Up”
what_it_measured: Longitudinal accent change of individuals filmed from childhood to adulthood.
key_finding_with_numbers: Shows individuals change vowel features after adolescence, complicating apparent-time assumptions (abstract). Numbers UNVERIFIED.
why_it_matters_for_sound_local: Evidence adults retain accent plasticity, which Sound Local relies on.

title: Ethnolects and the city: Ethnic orientation and linguistic variation in Toronto English
authors: Hoffman, Michol F.; Walker, James A.
what_it_measured: Linguistic variables across generations and ethnic orientation (variable list UNVERIFIED).
key_finding_with_numbers: First-generation speakers show L1 transfer; later generations largely converge, with ethnic orientation linked to rates for some variables (abstract). Rates UNVERIFIED.
why_it_matters_for_sound_local: Core paper on how ethnicity shapes Toronto English; MTE "local" sound is heritage-linked, not one standard.

title: ‘If ur from Toronto you’ll understand’: register change and metadiscursive engagement with mediatized Multicultural Toronto English
what_it_measured: How MTE is discussed and stylised on social media (enregisterment).
key_finding_with_numbers: Documents MTE as a register associated with racialised Toronto youth and its spread via online metadiscourse (abstract).
why_it_matters_for_sound_local: Shows what Torontonians themselves treat as MTE markers; ground truth for MTE content and respectful framing.

title: Heritage Tagalog Phonology and a Variationist Framework of Language Contact
accents: Toronto heritage Tagalog speakers vs Manila
what_it_measured: Rhotic realisation in heritage Tagalog in Toronto.
key_finding_with_numbers: About 3,000 /r/ tokens from 23 Toronto heritage speakers and 9 Manila speakers; approximant [ɹ] more common in 2nd generation and in speakers using more English (abstract).
why_it_matters_for_sound_local: Evidence of English /r/ transfer in Toronto's Filipino community; relevant to MTE-style multilingual input.

title: The private life of stops: VOT in a real-time corpus of spontaneous Glaswegian
authors: Stuart-Smith, Jane; Sonderegger, Morgan; Rathcke, Tamara; Macdonald, Rachel
what_it_measured: VOT of voiceless stops in spontaneous Glaswegian across decades, semi-automated measurement.
key_finding_with_numbers: Glaswegian /p t k/ range from vernacular short-lag (unaspirated) to more aspirated Scottish Standard English (abstract). VOT ms values UNVERIFIED.
why_it_matters_for_sound_local: Short-lag VOT is a measurable Glasgow cue; semi-automatic VOT method is phone-feasible.

title: The role of gesture delay in coda /r/ weakening: An articulatory, auditory and acoustic study
authors: Lawson, Eleanor; Stuart-Smith, Jane; Scobbie, James M.
venue: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
what_it_measured: Ultrasound tongue gesture timing, auditory and acoustic rhoticity of coda /r/.
key_finding_with_numbers: Delayed tongue-gesture timing links to weaker acoustic and perceived rhoticity, differing between Central Scottish sociolects (abstract). Which groups and measures UNVERIFIED.
why_it_matters_for_sound_local: Glasgow /r/ is sociolect-dependent; a single "rhotic=Scottish" F3 rule will mis-score some local speakers.

title: Bunched /r/ promotes vowel merger to schwar: An ultrasound tongue imaging study of Scottish sociophonetic variation
authors: Lawson, Eleanor; Scobbie, James M.; Stuart-Smith, Jane
what_it_measured: Ultrasound of bunched vs tip-up /r/ and pre-/r/ vowel mergers.
key_finding_with_numbers: Bunched /r/ associated with merger of pre-rhotic vowels to a rhotic schwa/syllabic /r/ (abstract). Proportions UNVERIFIED.
why_it_matters_for_sound_local: Pre-/r/ vowels (e.g. "bird", "word") need Scottish-specific targets.

title: On the Tail of the Scottish Vowel Length Rule in Glasgow
authors: Rathcke, Tamara V.; Stuart-Smith, Jane H.
what_it_measured: Durations of /i u a/ under the Scottish Vowel Length Rule across four speaker groups.
key_finding_with_numbers: Durational analyses of /i u a/ across 1970s and 2000s Glaswegian (full text); SVLR may be weakening via dialect contact and prosody (abstract). ms values UNVERIFIED.
why_it_matters_for_sound_local: SVLR (short "feed" vs long "freeze") is a duration cue robust to phone mics; this paper says how strong it really is today.

title: Structured Heterogeneity in Scottish Stops Over the Twentieth Century
authors: Sonderegger, Morgan; Stuart-Smith, Jane; Knowles, Thea; Macdonald, Rachel; Rathcke, Tamara
what_it_measured: VOT and voicing cues of stops across speakers and decades.
key_finding_with_numbers: Stop-voicing contrast varies in structured ways across speakers, linked to sound change (abstract). Estimates UNVERIFIED.
why_it_matters_for_sound_local: Calibrates how much stop variation counts as still local.

title: Intonational diglossia: a case study of Glasgow
venue: Journal of the International Phonetic Association
what_it_measured: Intonation of conversational vs read Glaswegian.
key_finding_with_numbers: Conversational Glaswegian uses a distinct local intonation while read speech resembles standard British (RP-like) intonation (abstract). Contour inventory UNVERIFIED.
why_it_matters_for_sound_local: Glasgow melody shows up in conversational, not read, prompts; game prompts should be conversational.

title: Structural and dialectal effects on pitch peak alignment in two varieties of British English
authors: Ladd, D.R.; Schepman, Astrid; White, Laurence; Quarmby, Louise May; Stackhouse, Rebekah
accents: Scottish Standard English vs Southern British English
what_it_measured: Pitch-peak alignment in nuclear and prenuclear accents.
key_finding_with_numbers: Reports dialectal differences in peak alignment between the two varieties (abstract). Direction and ms values UNVERIFIED.
why_it_matters_for_sound_local: Peak timing is a pitch cue that differentiates Scottish from Southern British melody.

title: The influence of Gujarati and Tamil L1s on Indian English: a preliminary study
authors: Wiltshire, Caroline R.; Harnsberger, James D.
what_it_measured: Consonants, vowels and intonation of 5 Gujarati and 5 Tamil L1 speakers of English.
key_finding_with_numbers: Some features shared (pan-Indian), others reflect L1 transfer (abstract). Feature counts UNVERIFIED.
why_it_matters_for_sound_local: Indian English is not one target; Mumbai (Marathi/Gujarati/Hindi) speakers may differ from Tamil speakers.

title: Homogeneity vs Heterogeneity in Indian English: Investigating Influences of L1 on f0 Range
authors: Maxwell, Olga; Payne, Elinor; Billington, Rosey
accents: Indian English (Telugu, Tamil, Hindi, Bengali L1)
what_it_measured: Pitch level, span and dynamism of educated Indian English speakers by L1.
key_finding_with_numbers: Tests whether f0 range is homogeneous across L1 groups (abstract). Semitone values UNVERIFIED.
why_it_matters_for_sound_local: Pitch range is a cheap phone-robust feature; this shows whether one Indian English pitch target is valid.

title: Speech Rhythm in Varieties of English
what_it_measured: Speech rhythm metrics (durational variability, accentual vs syllable timing) in varieties of English.
key_finding_with_numbers: Monograph; rhythm results UNVERIFIED (no abstract retrieved).
why_it_matters_for_sound_local: Main reference for measuring Indian English syllable-timed rhythm.

title: The “Indian English” of Tibeto-Burman language speakers
venue: English World-Wide. A Journal of Varieties of English
accents: Indian English of Angami, Ao, Mizo (Tibeto-Burman) L1 speakers
what_it_measured: Phonetic and phonological features of English by Northeast Indian speakers.
key_finding_with_numbers: Describes features and compares with mainstream Indian English (abstract). Numbers UNVERIFIED.
why_it_matters_for_sound_local: Further evidence that Indian English varies by L1; supports a Mumbai-specific target.

title: [v]at is going on? Local and global ideologies about Indian English
what_it_measured: /v/~/w/ realisation and its local vs global social meanings.
key_finding_with_numbers: [w]-like /v/ is a salient, ideologically loaded Indian English marker (abstract). Rates UNVERIFIED. Free repository link timed out on 2026-11-19 check (UNVERIFIED); DOI works.
why_it_matters_for_sound_local: Salient markers are what listeners hear as "Indian"; also flags sensitivity for respectful design.

title: Style repertoire and social change in British Asian English
what_it_measured: Ethnically marked phonetic variants across speakers' style repertoires.
key_finding_with_numbers: Speakers shift between Indian-like and British variants by context; interviews alone underestimate this (abstract).
why_it_matters_for_sound_local: Shows London itself includes Indian-origin features; MLE/London and Indian targets overlap.

title: Acoustic properties of the monophthongs of Assamese Indian English speakers
what_it_measured: Acoustic monophthongs of 20 Assamese speakers by medium of education.
key_finding_with_numbers: Vowel space differs by medium of education (abstract). Formant values UNVERIFIED.
why_it_matters_for_sound_local: Education/medium shapes Indian English vowels; useful for choosing reference speakers.

title: Reversing “drift”: Innovation and diffusion in the London diphthong system
authors: Paul E. Kerswill; Eivind Nessa Torgersen; Susan Patricia Fox
topic: London, MLE and Southern British English
what_it_measured: PRICE, MOUTH, FACE, GOAT diphthongs across age, ethnicity, area.
key_finding_with_numbers: Young inner-London speakers reverse the long-running diphthong-shift "drift", with innovations linked to multiethnic social networks (abstract). Specific vowel qualities and formant values UNVERIFIED.
why_it_matters_for_sound_local: Defines what young London actually sounds like; Cockney-style targets would be outdated.
region: London, MLE and Southern British English

title: An investigation of speech rhythm in London English
topic: London, MLE and Southern British English
what_it_measured: Speech rhythm metrics in London English.
key_finding_with_numbers: Inner London/MLE rhythm more syllable-timed than outer London (UNVERIFIED: abstract not retrieved).
why_it_matters_for_sound_local: Rhythm separates MLE from other London speech.
region: London, MLE and Southern British English

title: Individual profiles amidst a multiethnolect: Acoustic hetereogeneity in London English
authors: Kerswill, Paul; Gibson, Andy; Sharma, Devyani; McCarthy, Kathleen; Passoni, Elisa; Hellmuth, Sam
venue: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
topic: London, MLE and Southern British English
accents: Multicultural London English vs Standard Southern British
what_it_measured: Acoustic vowel profiles of individual MLE speakers.
key_finding_with_numbers: MLE is systematic yet heterogeneous across individuals (abstract). Numbers UNVERIFIED.
why_it_matters_for_sound_local: Score must accept a range of MLE realisations, not one mean.
region: London, MLE and Southern British English

title: Formant frequencies of RP monophthongs in four age groups of speakers
venue: Journal of the International Phonetic Association
topic: London, MLE and Southern British English
what_it_measured: F1/F2 of 11 RP monophthongs across four age groups of male speakers.
key_finding_with_numbers: 880 recorded items, 11 monophthongs, four age groups (abstract); age-related shifts present, specific vowels/values UNVERIFIED.
why_it_matters_for_sound_local: Shows how SSBE vowels shifted; modern references needed.
region: London, MLE and Southern British English

title: Variation and change in the<scp>trap</scp>and<scp>strut</scp>vowels of RP: a real time comparison of five acoustic data sets
venue: Journal of the International Phonetic Association
topic: London, MLE and Southern British English
what_it_measured: TRAP and STRUT positions, measured by angle and distance.
key_finding_with_numbers: Real-time change in TRAP/STRUT relationship (abstract). Values UNVERIFIED.
why_it_matters_for_sound_local: A geometry measure (angle/distance between vowels) is normalisation-friendly, like ACCDIST.
region: London, MLE and Southern British English

title: Compensation for coarticulation, /u/-fronting, and sound change in standard southern British: An acoustic and perceptual study
authors: Harrington, Jonathan; Kleber, Felicitas; Reubold, Ulrich
venue: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
topic: London, MLE and Southern British English
what_it_measured: GOOSE /u/-fronting in production and perception by age.
key_finding_with_numbers: Younger speakers front /u/ and listeners' compensation for coarticulation tracks this (abstract). Values UNVERIFIED.
why_it_matters_for_sound_local: GOOSE fronting is a strong Southern British cue.
region: London, MLE and Southern British English

title: A cross-dialectal acoustic comparison of vowels in Northern and Southern British English
venue: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
topic: London, MLE and Southern British English
what_it_measured: Duration, F1, F2 and DCT trajectories for 11 monophthongs and 5 diphthongs.
key_finding_with_numbers: Significant dialect differences in several vowels incl. dynamic trajectories (abstract). Values UNVERIFIED.
why_it_matters_for_sound_local: Supports measuring trajectories (DCT), not just midpoints.
region: London, MLE and Southern British English

title: Social Salience and the Sociolinguistic Monitor
topic: London, MLE and Southern British English
what_it_measured: Listener sensitivity to frequency of two variables differing in social salience.
key_finding_with_numbers: 149 British listeners; sensitivity to variant frequency differed by variable's salience (abstract).
why_it_matters_for_sound_local: Not all features count equally; weight salient ones (e.g. TH-fronting) higher.
region: London, MLE and Southern British English

title: A typology of laterals in twelve English dialects
authors: Kirkham, Sam; Turton, Danielle; Leemann, Adrian
venue: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
topic: London, MLE and Southern British English
what_it_measured: Onset vs coda /l/ acoustics from crowdsourced smartphone recordings.
key_finding_with_numbers: 95 speakers across 12 dialects; three main onset/coda lateral patterns (abstract).
why_it_matters_for_sound_local: Smartphone-collected data still yields dialect-level /l/ differences; usable feature.
region: London, MLE and Southern British English

title: Towards an updated dialect atlas of British English
authors: MacKenzie, Laurel; Bailey, George; Turton, Danielle
topic: London, MLE and Southern British English
what_it_measured: Crowdsourced survey of 12 phonological, lexical and morphosyntactic variables.
key_finding_with_numbers: Over 14,000 responses; maps 12 variables (abstract).
why_it_matters_for_sound_local: Current geography of features, incl. BATH/TRAP and others; update to Trudgill-era maps.
region: London, MLE and Southern British English

title: The beauty in a beast: Minimising the effects of diverse recording quality on vowel formant measurements in sociophonetic real-time studies
authors: Rathcke, Tamara; Stuart-Smith, Jane; Torsney, Bernard; Harrington, Jonathan
what_it_measured: Effect of diverse recording quality on formant measurements; compares normalisations.
key_finding_with_numbers: Compared Lobanov, Nearey, Watt-Fabricius, distance-ratio and statistical estimation against raw Bark (full text); some methods better reduced technical artefacts (abstract).
why_it_matters_for_sound_local: Directly about making formant scores robust to bad recordings.

title: Remote sociophonetic data collection: Vowels and nasalization over video conferencing apps
venue: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
what_it_measured: Zoom, Skype, Teams vs professional and iPad recordings.
key_finding_with_numbers: Compared vowel configurations, mergers and nasalisation across apps vs professional/iPad recordings (abstract). Which measures were distorted and by how much UNVERIFIED.
why_it_matters_for_sound_local: Compression artefacts vary by app; avoid nasality-type features.

title: (Don't) Try this at Home! The Effects of Recording Devices and Software on Phonetic Analysis
authors: Sanker, Chelsea; Babinski, Sarah; Burns, Roslyn; Evans, Marisha; Johns, Jeremy; Kim, Juhyae; Smith, Slater; Weber, Natalie; Bowern, Claire
what_it_measured: Effects of recording devices and software on phonetic measures.
key_finding_with_numbers: Devices and software substantially altered frequency, duration and noise measurements (abstract). Values UNVERIFIED.
why_it_matters_for_sound_local: Quantifies the device bias Sound Local must cancel.

title: Comparing acoustic analyses of speech data collected remotely
authors: Zhang, Cong; Jepson, Kathleen; Lohfink, Georg; Arvaniti, Amalia
venue: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
what_it_measured: Remote recording via phones, laptops and Zoom vs Zoom H6 recorder.
key_finding_with_numbers: F0 tracked accurately by all devices; phones closer than Zoom to the H6 for F1–F3 (abstract).
why_it_matters_for_sound_local: Phone mic recording is acceptable for F0 and formants; streaming apps are worse.

title: Is Zoom viable for sociophonetic research? A comparison of in-person and online recordings for vocalic analysis
authors: Calder, Jeremy; Wheeler, Rebecca; Adams, Sarah; Amarelo, Daniel; Arnold-Murray, Katherine; Bai, Justin; Church, Meredith; Daniels, Josh; Gomez, Sarah; Henry, Jacob; Jia, Yunan; Johnson-Morris, Brienna; Lee, Kyo; Miller, Kit; Powell, Derrek; Ramsey-Smith, Caitlin; Rayl, Sydney; Rosenau, Sara; Salvador, Nadine
what_it_measured: Zoom vs in-person recordings of vowels.
key_finding_with_numbers: Zoom gave lower raw F1 and higher F2; discrepancies remained after normalisation (abstract).
why_it_matters_for_sound_local: Normalisation does not fully remove channel bias; calibrate per device.

title: Crowdsourcing Language Change with Smartphone Applications
authors: Leemann, Adrian; Kolly, Marie-José; Purves, Ross; Britain, David; Glaser, Elvira
what_it_measured: Smartphone app predicting dialect from 16 variables.
key_finding_with_numbers: Data from nearly 60,000 speakers; 16 variables (full text).
why_it_matters_for_sound_local: Proof that a playful phone dialect app gathers large, analysable data.

title: Smartphone Recordings are Comparable to “Gold Standard” Recordings for Acoustic Measurements of Voice
authors: Awan, Shaheen N.; Shaikh, Mohsin Ahmed; Awan, Jordan A.; Abdalla, Ibrahim; Lim, Kelvin O.; Misono, Stephanie
what_it_measured: iPhone and Samsung recordings vs studio across rooms and distances.
key_finding_with_numbers: 24 diverse speakers; smartphone acoustic voice measures comparable to gold standard (abstract). Agreement statistics UNVERIFIED.
why_it_matters_for_sound_local: Supports phone-mic f0 and voice-quality measures.

title: Comparing measurement errors for formants in synthetic and natural vowels
authors: Shadle, Christine H.; Nam, Hosung; Whalen, D. H.
venue: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
what_it_measured: Formant measurement error vs F0 for manual and automatic methods.
key_finding_with_numbers: Measurement bias depends on F0 (abstract); prior literature reports about ±60 Hz F1/F2 LPC error for F0 100–300 Hz (full text). New error values UNVERIFIED.
why_it_matters_for_sound_local: High-pitched voices (women, children) get worse formants; widen tolerance or weight by F0.

title: Fast Track: fast (nearly) automatic formant-tracking using Praat
what_it_measured: Fast Track: Praat formant tracker choosing among multiple analyses.
key_finding_with_numbers: Selects smoothest candidate track and outputs formants, bandwidths, F0 and logs (abstract).
why_it_matters_for_sound_local: Multiple-candidate formant tracking reduces tracking errors on phone audio.

title: Improving the Consistency of Formant Measurement
authors: Duckworth, Martin; McDougall, Kirsty; de Jong, Gea; Shockey, Linda
venue: The International Journal of Speech, Language and the Law
what_it_measured: Inter-analyst formant consistency across three labs.
key_finding_with_numbers: 40 British male speakers, six monophthongs, six repetitions; common procedures reduced but did not remove differences (abstract).
why_it_matters_for_sound_local: Even experts disagree on formants; the score needs tolerance bands.

title: A comparison of three speaker-intrinsic vowel formant frequency normalization algorithms for sociophonetics
authors: Anne H. Fabricius; Dominic J. L. Watt; Daniel Ezra Johnson
what_it_measured: Compares Watt-Fabricius S-centroid with Lobanov and Nearey normalisation.
key_finding_with_numbers: Modified W&F performs between Lobanov and Nearey, sometimes as well as both (full text).
why_it_matters_for_sound_local: Picks the normalisation for comparing a player to a local reference.

title: The ΔF method of vocal tract length normalization for vowels
venue: Laboratory Phonology: Journal of the Association for Laboratory Phonology
what_it_measured: ΔF vocal-tract-length normalisation from average formant spacing.
key_finding_with_numbers: Method normalises using a single speaker scale factor (abstract).
why_it_matters_for_sound_local: Works from few vowels; suited to short game sessions.

title: A regression approach to vowel normalization for missing and unbalanced data
venue: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
what_it_measured: Regression-based normalisation for missing/unbalanced vowel data.
key_finding_with_numbers: Compares log-mean and Lobanov; proposes regression approach for unbalanced data (abstract).
why_it_matters_for_sound_local: Players produce uneven vowel sets; this method handles that.

title: Performance analysis of several pitch detection algorithms on simulated and real noisy speech data
what_it_measured: Pitch trackers on simulated and real noisy speech.
key_finding_with_numbers: Real public-place noise behaved like clean speech plus babble noise (abstract). Error rates UNVERIFIED.
why_it_matters_for_sound_local: Choose a pitch tracker tested in real noise.

title: Today’s Most Frequently Used F0 Estimation Methods, and Their Accuracy in Estimating Male and Female Pitch in Clean Speech
what_it_measured: Accuracy of common F0 estimators for male and female voices.
key_finding_with_numbers: Praat most accurate; setting pitch range by gender improved accuracy (abstract TLDR).
why_it_matters_for_sound_local: Set F0 range per player before scoring melody.

title: PEFAC - A Pitch Estimation Algorithm Robust to High Levels of Noise
venue: IEEE/ACM Transactions on Audio, Speech, and Language Processing
what_it_measured: PEFAC pitch estimator for high noise.
key_finding_with_numbers: Designed for high noise levels via normalisation, harmonic summing and voicing probability (abstract). Error rates UNVERIFIED.
why_it_matters_for_sound_local: Candidate pitch tracker for noisy phone audio.

title: Beware of the ‘telephone effect’: the influence of telephone transmission on the measurement of formant frequencies
venue: International Journal of Speech, Language and the Law
what_it_measured: Telephone transmission effect on formants.
key_finding_with_numbers: Telephone band-pass attenuates low frequencies and raises measured F1 (abstract). Size UNVERIFIED.
why_it_matters_for_sound_local: Phone codecs shift F1; calibrate rather than compare raw Hz.
